title: Theme system: make tokens swappable so dark mode can be added later with minimal effort (no per-component changes)
description:
USER REQUEST: ensure a real theme system is in place so dark-mode support can be re-added in the future with reasonable effort. Do NOT change the current LIGHT Flash 8 appearance — just make it swappable.

CONTEXT: packages/authoring-ui/src/theme/flash8Theme.ts exports semantic tokens (chrome.*, halo.*, content.*) + helpers (panelStyle/titleBarStyle/buttonStyle/inputStyle/bevel/chromeFont/widgetFont). ~40 components already import these. The hard requirement: enabling dark mode later must NOT require editing all 40 components again.

REQUIREMENTS:
1. PRESERVE the public export surface EXACTLY (same token names/shape, same helper signatures) so all existing importers (and 3 in-flight bugfix agents importing it read-only) keep compiling unchanged.
2. Introduce a Theme abstraction: a typed Theme shape; a  value-set (the CURRENT values) and a  value-set (reconstruct the pre-re-theme dark palette — old values are in git history: chrome ~#1a1a1a/#2a2a2a/#3c3c3c bg, #555 borders, #e0e0e0/#c0c0c0 text, the old accent #1a6ea8; build a coherent dark set). 
3. SWAP MECHANISM for DOM-consumed tokens (chrome/halo): back them with CSS custom properties — inject a stylesheet defining the light values on :root (and dark values under a  selector), and make the exported chrome/halo token strings resolve to  (with the light hex as fallback). Because components reference the SAME token constants, flipping  swaps the whole DOM UI with ZERO component edits. Keep the light fallback so nothing changes by default.
4. CANVAS/content colors (content.* used by StageArea/Timeline canvas drawing need REAL hex, not var()): provide a theme-aware resolver — e.g. an  accessor + a subscribe/notify or a  that reads the current mode — so canvas redraws pick up the active theme. Keep content.* returning concrete light hex by default. Document that canvas consumers read via the resolver to be theme-reactive.
5. Provide a minimal switch API: a  (sets the data-theme attr + active JS theme + triggers canvas re-render via a notify) and/or a ThemeProvider + useTheme() hook. DEFAULT = light (Flash 8). Do not add a UI toggle (out of scope) — just the capability + maybe a Preferences hook left as a TODO.
6. VERIFY light is visually UNCHANGED: build + all authoring-ui tests green (only ~3 task-1207 fixture failures acceptable); ideally confirm computed colors of a couple surfaces are identical to before (e.g. panel bg still #ECECEC). Optionally smoke-test that setting data-theme=dark actually changes a sampled bg (proves swappability) then revert.
7. DOCUMENT in docs/30-flash8-ui-spec.md (or a new docs/31-theming.md): the theme architecture and the exact bounded steps to fully enable dark mode (fill/adjust flash8Dark values + add a Preferences toggle calling setThemeMode).

Scope: packages/authoring-ui/src/theme/* (+ a CSS file + a tiny provider/hook + docs). Minimize/avoid edits to component files — the whole point is that components don't need touching. ACQUIRE lock; commit incl task file; push rebase-retry. Coordinate: preserve the export surface so concurrent importers don't break.
